clue.text: Captain's given fish but not head

indicators.note: losing its head means the opening letter of the captain's title is dropped

parts.note: a skipper is the captain of a boat or team

explanation.surface: A ship's captain is handed a fish, minus its head, as a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A kipper is a smoked herring, a common breakfast fish in Britain.

clue.text: Endless drink making one do this?

indicators.note: endless says the drink word loses its final letter

parts.note: to slurp is to drink noisily

explanation.surface: A drink that never runs dry might leave the drinker mumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest of the clue: too much drink makes one speak indistinctly, which is to do this.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy drinking leads people to run their words together, so the drunkard's speech is the act described.

clue.text: Vain son I ordered to get occupation

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A vain son is told to go and find himself a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occupation' looks like a job; here it is the military sense of taking over a territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Military occupation follows an armed entry into a country, so the two are synonyms in this sense.

clue.text: Look about five, and go hungry

indicators.note: about means the looking word goes around the numeral

parts.note: to stare is to look fixedly
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Someone appears to be about five years old and is going without food.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to suffer from lack of food, a stronger form of going hungry.

clue.text: Present going with birthday suit

definitions.meaning: physically there, in person rather than in spirit
going about naked, wearing only the skin one was born in

explanation.surface: A gift that comes with a naked outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in person, and taken literally describes bare skin with no clothes.

clue.text: They take care of the draught but also sink the spirits

definitions.text: They take care of the draught but also sink the spirits

parts.words: They take care of the draught but also sink the spirits
parts.note: sounds like people who block draughts and lower morale, but describes people who down draught beer and knock back spirits

explanation.surface: Household helpers who stop cold air but dampen everyone's mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take care of' is slang for dealing with something by finishing it off; 'sink' is slang for swallowing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: People who consume draught beer and spirits are the ones who imbibe alcohol.

clue.text: Vincent accepts Leo running wild in brutality

indicators.note: accepts means the name takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: Vince is the short form of the name Vincent

indicators.note: running wild says the letters of Leo are scrambled

explanation.surface: Vincent takes in a man called Leo who is out of control and violent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running wild' looks like part of the surface's brutality, but it only scrambles the name Leo; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutality is savage physical force, which is a synonym for violent conduct.

clue.text: Quarrel — and produce sword?

definitions.meaning: to argue or have a row with someone
jumbling the letters of words gives sword, so changing words produces it

explanation.surface: An argument escalates until someone draws a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading angry remarks is an idiom for arguing, and literally altering the letters of 'words' yields 'sword'.

clue.text: Plain central stretch of inlet undrained

indicators.note: central stretch of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A description of the flat ground in the middle of a marshy inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Plain central' as the definition, but tundra lies in the Arctic, not centrally; 'central' belongs with 'stretch of' as the hiding signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is a vast treeless Arctic plain, so it is an example of flat open land.

clue.text: Ancient city, not all in South Africa

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a part is not all of something

explanation.surface: An old city, only partly located in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was a powerful city state of ancient Greece, famed for its warriors.

clue.text: Device used when travelling from Cape Horn?

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters move about and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: Asks what gadget a sailor would use on the road from the tip of South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A car phone is a gadget for calls fitted in a vehicle, used on the move.

clue.text: Tom caught in falsehood after outing in three parts

indicators.note: after means the falsehood part comes after the outing word

parts.note: a trip is an outing or excursion

indicators.note: caught in means the animal is held inside the falsehood word

parts.note: a lie is a falsehood
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Someone named Tom is caught out lying after a day trip, in a three-part story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a name but is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Documents made in triplicate exist as three identical copies, so the phrase means threefold.

clue.text: Racing foolishly, tense at first but no longer concerned

indicators.note: at first says the tense word goes before the rest

parts.note: the past is a grammatical tense

indicators.note: foolishly says the letters of racing are jumbled

explanation.surface: A driver racing recklessly is nervous at first but later stops worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like nervous; it is the grammatical tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beyond worry about something is an idiom for no longer caring at all.

clue.text: Charged for fodder

definitions.meaning: having had a fee set, or been billed

explanation.definitionFit: Animal fodder is feed, and to be feed is to have been charged a fee.

clue.text: Chatter disturbed tragedian's waffle

parts.note: gas is idle talk or chatter

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of tragedians are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Chit-chat unsettles an actor's long-winded speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for pompous empty talk, so it is a synonym for verbose nonsense.

clue.text: Doctor gives our outcome to be severe

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A physician delivers a serious result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person; it is the verb meaning to tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: Grievous injuries are serious ones, so it is a synonym for grave or harsh.

clue.text: Bagged up very soon?

definitions.meaning: put inside a Jiffy, a British brand of padded mailing envelope

explanation.surface: Something wrapped up and promised for delivery shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jiffy bag is a padded envelope, a brand familiar in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means almost immediately, and literally describes something packed in that padded envelope.

clue.text: Find out about scrapping over record

indicators.note: scrapping means the word over is removed from the find-out word

parts.note: to discover is to find out

explanation.surface: Someone investigates the scrapping of a recording.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record or other recording, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Shabby fluff behind foot?

parts.note: down is soft fluffy feathers or hair
at heel means close behind someone's feet, as a dog walks

explanation.surface: Asks whether scruffy means fluff stuck behind the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes worn-out shoes and so a shabby, neglected appearance.

clue.text: Gloomy organ in arid setting

indicators.note: in means the organ goes inside the arid word

parts.note: arid means dry
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A church organ sits in a dry, bleak place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the instrument; it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary means dull and depressing, a synonym of gloomy.

clue.text: Looking towards heaven, person that's holy and chaste spouts

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking upward means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy person
chaste means pure

explanation.surface: A pious, chaste person gazes up to heaven and sounds off.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano that erupts spouts lava, so the verbs are synonyms of gushing out.

clue.text: Eavesdrop in this direction, you say?

indicators.note: you say signals the words are as spoken, a soundalike

parts.note: over here means to this place, this way

explanation.surface: Someone invites a listener to come and spy this way.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop is to listen in secretly, which is to hear something by chance or stealth.

clue.text: Flood at home, getting cross after complaint

indicators.note: after means the cross letter follows the illness

parts.note: in means at home
flu is a complaint, an illness
X is a cross shape

explanation.surface: A homeowner with flu gets angry about a flooded house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' looks like a grumble; it is an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: An influx is a large inflow of people or things, a synonym of flood in that sense.

clue.text: Lies if coming up with abuse regularly

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read upwards
regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Untruths emerge along with constant abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibs are small untruths, a synonym for lies.

clue.text: Go with Queen's painter

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An artist goes along with the monarch, as her official painter.
explanation.definitionFit: J M W Turner was a celebrated English landscape artist.

clue.text: Sure things should be secure, organised best

parts.note: safe means secure

indicators.note: organised says the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Certainties ought to be protected, with the best arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Safe bets are wagers or outcomes certain to succeed, synonyms of certainties.
